summary: v_-driven fix property/global values are re-evaluated every N steps but never reach contact models during a run: the registry copies coefficients (Yeff, Geff, betaeff, coeffRestLog, coeffFrict, cohesion/adhesion/surface energy) once per run at Force::init
failure_scenario: Deck with coefficientRestitution v_e (e: 0.9 -> 0.5 at t=0.05 s) keeps e=0.9 for the rest of the run; chute_wear_hpc prints decaying v_cor/v_mu/v_adh in thermo while the model uses frozen values; fix check/timestep/gran and mesh k_finnie (raw pointers) do see updates -> inconsistent state
recommendation: Either (a) make update_variable_values() mark the registry dirty and re-run creators for affected properties (and re-connect pointers) before the next pair compute, or (b) error at init if a v_ entry feeds a registry property until (a) exists. Document the energy consequences of stiffness changes for existing contacts (history spring stores displacement).

summary: Neighbor::trigger_build() is rank-local: fix adapt/liggghts sets force_rebuild from a per-rank max growth without MPI_Allreduce, so decide() returns different values on different ranks -> ranks enter exchange/borders vs forward_comm -> deadlock
failure_scenario: 2 ranks, rank 1 owns no particles (normal for DEM insertion), radius growth >= skin/2 per application: run hangs after step 10 until killed; identical deck with atoms on both ranks finishes in 0.8 ms
recommendation: MPI_Allreduce(MAX) the growth in FixAdaptLiggghts::apply() before calling trigger_build(); additionally make Neighbor::decide() reduce force_rebuild (MPI_MAX) or document that trigger_build() must be called collectively.

summary: Radius growth beyond the run-init maximum radius is invisible to bins/stencils/ghost cutoff (cutneighmax from maxrad_dynamic at init); rebuilds do not help -> contacts silently missed
failure_scenario: Two spheres 5 mm apart grow r 1->3 mm (1 mm overlap): zero force, zero KE, 7 rebuilds; in parallel the ghost shell is also too thin
recommendation: Require a max_radius keyword (or evaluate the variable bound) and implement use_rad_for_cut_neigh_and_ghost()/max_rad(type) so PairGran::init_style sizes cutneighmax/cutghost; error at runtime if any radius exceeds it.

summary: Trigger criterion uses growth since the previous application (not cumulative since last build) and ignores displacement; redundant with legacy rhold-aware check_distance when every=1, insufficient when neigh_modify every>1/delay>0/check no
failure_scenario: neigh_modify every 10 check yes and growth 0.3*skin per application: accumulated growth + displacement exceeds skin/2 between checks -> missed contacts (dangerous builds)
recommendation: Remove trigger_build() from the fix and rely on check_distance (radvary path), or track cumulative growth since Neighbor::lastcall and test |dx|+dr against skin/2 exactly like check_distance.

summary: Radius/rmass changed in pre_force after the step's forward comm: ghosts keep old radius for that step's force evaluation; with newton off the two ranks compute F_ij with different radii (non-antisymmetric), results depend on rank count
failure_scenario: Any multi-rank run with fix adapt/liggghts: one-step momentum error at every adapt step for boundary pairs; trajectories differ between 1 and N ranks beyond summation-order effects
recommendation: Call comm->forward_comm() (radvary forward packs radius+rmass) at the end of apply(); add a rank-count reproducibility test.

summary: For shape/volume/inertia atoms (superquadric) inertia is overwritten with the ellipsoid formula 0.2 m(b^2+c^2) (wrong unless blockiness=2), atom->area is not rescaled, and superquadric AtomVec keeps radvary=0 so ghost radius/shape are not forward-communicated
failure_scenario: Superquadric (cube-like, blockiness 8) with fix adapt/liggghts: moment of inertia wrong by ~35-60 %, rotational dynamics silently wrong; ghost shape stale until reneighbor
recommendation: Reject superquadric/multisphere at init until supported, or compute inertia/area via MathExtraLiggghtsNonspherical superquadric routines and implement radvary forward comm for AtomVecSuperquadric.

summary: Radius growth injects elastic energy (overlap), mass change at fixed v changes momentum/KE, no Rayleigh/Hertz timestep re-check, no guard for multisphere/rigid bodies
failure_scenario: Touching spheres grown by 1 % separate at ~0.1 m/s (KE 1.04e-7 J vs 1.18e-7 J Hertz overlap energy); chute_wear_hpc KE drops 1.1 % at run-2 setup; chute_wear_hpc end state dt ~ 87 % of Rayleigh time
recommendation: Document; optionally cap per-step overlap increase; recompute Rayleigh dt when radius/density changes (warn/error); error if fix multisphere/rigid present.

summary: clamp_value silently clamps literals and variable values (e>1 -> 1, mu<0 -> 0) with no warning; clamp range [0,1] disagrees with registry sanity (0.05,1]; e clamped to 0 gives log(0)=-inf -> betaeff NaN where sanity checks are off
failure_scenario: Old deck with coefficientRestitution 1.2 used to error, now silently runs with e=1; variable e decaying to 0 errors only at the next run
recommendation: Error (or at least warning once) instead of silent clamp; align bounds with the model sanity checks (e in (0,1]); never clamp literal input.

summary: 'every N' accepted without any v_ entry (silent no-op); write() dumps evaluated numbers and loses the v_ binding/every N; no restart record of variable bindings
failure_scenario: User writes fix ... youngsModulus peratomtype 5e6 every 100 believing it enables updates; file= output re-read later is static
recommendation: Error/warn on every without v_; write v_names and every N back in write().

summary: Latent: matrix grow() changes nvalues without resizing value_variable_names/indices (new) or values_recomputed/array_recomputed (legacy) -> destructor delete[] out of bounds
failure_scenario: Any future caller of FixPropertyGlobal::grow() on a matrix -> heap corruption at unfix/exit
recommendation: Replace raw arrays with std::vector<std::string>/std::vector<int> sized with nvalues and resize them in grow(); or delete grow() matrix branch (no callers).

summary: sync_recomputed_values() overwrites the entire values_recomputed on every update, clobbering values other fixes store via get_array_modified()/compute_*_modified
failure_scenario: fix heat/gran/conduction with youngsModulusOriginal given as v_ variable: deltan_ratio modifications reset each update
recommendation: Only copy entries that are variable-driven.

summary: ensure_variable_values_initialized() is reached from registry creators in Force::init before Modify::init; variables referencing c_ computes are evaluated before the compute is initialised
failure_scenario: equal-style variable using c_ID (e.g. temperature-dependent friction) -> crash or garbage on the first run
recommendation: Resolve indices only; defer evaluation to FixPropertyGlobal::init()/setup_pre_force; forbid c_ references in init-time evaluation.

summary: SoA path (off by default) triples memory traffic per half-step (AoS->SoA->AoS copies incl. unused x in final_integrate), kernels are not vectorized (mask branch), and only plain fix nve uses it (DEM uses nve/sphere) -> no achievable benefit
failure_scenario: Enabling LIGGGHTS_USE_SOA_NVE slows fix nve and does nothing for granular runs
recommendation: Delete aligned_particle_soa.h, FixNVE::soa_ and the #ifdef branches (report 14.1); if SoA is pursued, do it at AtomVec level with persistent storage (Cabana AoSoA as reference).

summary: SoA path is not bit-identical to AoS (dtf*(1/m) vs dtf/m: 24 % of velocity components differ after one step) and takes &vec[0] of an empty vector on ranks with nlocal==0 (UB; aborts with _GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS)
failure_scenario: Build with -DLIGGGHTS_USE_SOA_NVE: rank with no atoms aborts under debug STL; trajectories diverge from AoS at ULP level
recommendation: Use .data(); use division to match legacy if kept; preferably delete (F-15).

summary: No-op sync_linear/angular_sphere_soa() stubs called from 5 places; zero_rotation() calls the linear instead of the angular stub
failure_scenario: None today; misleading scaffolding for future SoA work
recommendation: Remove stubs and calls.

summary: fix_hdtorque_->array_atom is dereferenced whenever couple/cfd/force/implicit exists, but fix_hdtorque_ is only created when use_torque is set -> NULL dereference before the new scheme-4 check can fire (all schemes)
failure_scenario: nve/superquadric + couple/cfd/force/implicit without torque: segfault at first step
recommendation: Check the FixPropertyAtom pointers (not only their arrays) before dereferencing; move array lookup to init() with collective errors.

summary: Single negative deck with no runner/expected-output check; no tests for v_ properties, every N, fix adapt/liggghts, trigger_build, neighlist/mesh change, dump accessors, dump hdf5/mesh/hdf5
failure_scenario: Regressions in any of the reviewed features go unnoticed
recommendation: Adopt audit/cases/fixes/* as ctest regression cases with numeric pass criteria (see fixes_vv_requests.md).

summary: Undocumented semantic change: 'iAtom > nlocal' -> 'iAtom >= nlocal' (first ghost no longer treated as local). Correct off-by-one fix, benign for forces (fix_wall_gran skips iPart>=nlocal) but changes numAllContacts_/ghost nneighs; report calls the file change purely non-semantic
failure_scenario: Bitwise A/B vs HEAD may differ in mesh contact statistics
recommendation: Document in the modification report as a bug fix.

summary: With a '*' (multifile) filename every per-file XDMF lists all previously written steps but points them into the current file -> dangling references
failure_scenario: dump ... hdf5 10 post/multi_*.h5: multi_30.h5.xdmf references Step_0/10/20 in multi_30.h5 (18 missing refs)
recommendation: Store (filename step) pairs and write one temporal XDMF index that references the right file per step.

summary: XDMF DataItems omit NumberType/Precision -> readers default to Float32 (ids >2^24 inexact, positions truncated); Time Value is the timestep index, not simulation time
failure_scenario: VTK/ParaView XDMF reader loads id/position/velocity as float32; animations have time axis in steps
recommendation: Emit NumberType="Float" Precision="8" for doubles, NumberType="Int" Precision="8"/"4" for ids/connectivity; write Time=step*dt (store dt/time as attribute).

summary: First write of each dump instance truncates the file (no append), so a restarted job destroys earlier output; dump_modify sort/append/precision silently ignored; no type field, no image flags, no thresh/region
failure_scenario: Continuing a long chute run from restart with the same dump file name erases previous history
recommendation: Support append (open existing file and read existing Step_ groups); reject unsupported dump_modify keywords; add type/image.

summary: Return values of H5Dcreate/H5Dwrite/H5Sselect_*/H5Pset_chunk/H5Gcreate/H5Fclose are not checked; a failed write (quota, dataset exists) is silent
failure_scenario: Disk quota exhausted mid-run: simulation continues with corrupt/truncated HDF5 and no error
recommendation: Check every call and MPI_Allreduce an error flag -> error->all.

summary: XDMF sidecar rewritten in full at every dump (O(N^2) bytes) and HDF5 file re-opened collectively per dump
failure_scenario: chute_wear (2000 dumps) writes ~2.6 GB of XDMF text on rank 0 over the run
recommendation: Append grids incrementally (seek before closing tags) or write the XDMF once at the end/at checkpoints; keep the file open between dumps (H5Fflush).

summary: HDF5 support only via a Makefile with hard-coded OpenMPI include/lib paths and -march=native; no CMake option; no H5_HAVE_PARALLEL guard (serial HDF5 fails to compile/link obscurely)
failure_scenario: Build on a cluster with MPICH or serial HDF5 fails; binaries not portable across CPUs
recommendation: Add a CMake option LIGGGHTS_ENABLE_HDF5 using find_package(HDF5 COMPONENTS C) and HDF5_IS_PARALLEL; #error or serial fallback when !H5_HAVE_PARALLEL.

summary: Tutorial now requires the non-default hdf5mpi build (stock binary: 'Invalid dump style'); postscript expects dump*.chute; post/.gitignore placeholder deleted (fresh clone lacks post/ -> H5Fcreate fails); committed chute_particles.h5 is from an older deck (every 200); comment lists wrong fields. Run length 1e5->1e6 is justified (6000 particles at 0.1 kg/s need ~7.5 s) but 10x cost
failure_scenario: User runs the tutorial with the default build and it errors; fresh clone errors 'Cannot open parallel HDF5 dump file'
recommendation: Keep the VTK/custom dump as default and put HDF5 in a separate deck; restore post/.gitignore (with *.h5 *.xdmf rules); remove generated outputs from the tree.

summary: chute_wear_hpc demonstrates no-op variable properties (F-01), overwrites the particle size distribution with an equal-style radius (monodisperse r=9.96e-5 m at end), shrinks radius 20x so dt reaches ~87 % of the Rayleigh time, and was only run on 1 rank
failure_scenario: Users copy the 'HPC' example believing it validates time-dependent contact properties and parallel HDF5
recommendation: Rewrite: atom-style radius scaling (r*f(t)) instead of absolute equal-style radius, fix check/timestep/gran, a multi-rank run, and remove v_cor/v_mu until F-01 is fixed.

summary: [LEGACY] 'if(last_value_arg < 5+darg+nvalues)' is tautologically false; matrix style with zero values (e.g. 'matrix 2 every 5') is accepted silently; no restart support for fix property/global
failure_scenario: Malformed input accepted silently
recommendation: Check nvalues >= 1 explicitly.

summary: [LEGACY] Fix::global_freq defaults to 0 and FixPropertyGlobal never sets it: thermo f_ID[i][j] (or a variable referencing it) of a property/global -> integer divide by zero (SIGFPE)
failure_scenario: thermo_style custom ... f_m3[1][1] to monitor a v_-driven property -> crash in Thermo::init
recommendation: Set global_freq = 1 (or update_every) in FixPropertyGlobal constructor; guard modulo by zero in thermo/variable.
